pr_title: Allow users to set font features and font axes
pr_body:
Adds support for users to be able to set font features and axes (see the spec for more details!)

## Detailed Description

**CustomTextLayout**
- Asks the `DxFontRenderData` for the font features when getting glyphs
- _If any features have been set/updated, we always skip the "isTextSimple" shortcut_
- Asks the `_formatInUse` for any font axes when mapping characters in `_AnalyzeFontFallback`

**DxFontRenderData**
- Stores a map of font features (initialized to the [standard feature list])
- Stores a map of font axes
- Has methods to add font features/axes to the map or update existing ones
- Has methods to retrieve the font features/axes
- Sets the font axes in the `IDWriteTextFormat` when creating it

## Validation Steps Performed
It works!

[standard feature list]: https://github.com/fdwr/TextLayoutSampler/blob/ac5aef67d1cc0cb67c5e3be29b30bda5a90c3e2b/DrawableObject.ixx#L802

Specified in #10457
Related to #1790 
Closes #759
Closes #5828

Okay since there's been enough contention on whether we can unify `UpdateFont` with setting the font features/axes, the latest commit unifies them in the following way:

> I was thinking that it could be something like where UpdateFont just had optional parameters at the end that defaulted to nullptr for all the renderers except this one which would unify it all up into a single call ensuring that the update happens along with setting the properties, eliminates the need to pick out the specific derived type for the DX renderer, and would mean no changes really for the GDI and other renderers as they would default those parameters out.

If we feel like we're okay with the amount of diff this creates across all the renderers etc then alright, if not its an easy enough revert

> unify UpdateFont with setting the font features/axes,

Is it too late for me to say you can add them in FontInfoBase, like I said before? No change in the interface needed.

> > unify UpdateFont with setting the font features/axes,
> 
> Is it too late for me to say you can add them in FontInfoBase, like I said before? No change in the interface needed.

Okay, we probably have to have a discussion about this (@miniksa, @lhecker, @skyline75489)

Here's my reasons for not wanting it in FontInfo:

1. We do not need durable process-lifetime storage for an intermediate map of feature tags and axes _in conhost_ (not for VT, not for GDI, not for WDDM or BGFX, and conhost doesn't use DX today.)
   * If we were to store it, what form would it be?
      * We cannot store a vector of `DWRITE_THINGs` because this layer is insulated from DirectWrite; therefore we need to store the raw tag values
      * `unordered_map<wstring>` is wasteful in the empty case (most common in conhost), and this would grow every FontInfo by 128 bytes (amd64), and it may allocate to store the empty node; we would also have to store every feature and axis name, as the FontInfo would become the primary source (we couldn't store string_views)
      * `unordered_map<uint32_t>` works for storing them as non-strings, but they still cost the same (64 bytes for features, 64 for axes)
2. We have a long history of adding features specific to one rendering engine to the engine's local interface.

Heck, that's why I don't want it on `UpdateFont`, either. It's two optionals that will *never* be populated in conhost.

If the prevailing idea is that we should either violate FontInfo's agnosticness for whether it is DirectWrite-enabled, or store font feature tags in it directly¹, I'm happy to be overridden... but I don't see the cost for the benefit.

What does storing it in FontInfo get us?

¹ we would also have to move the weight/slant/italic/stretch converter into FontInfo...
FWIW: I am more okay with UpdateFont, but we are required to validate it against bgfx and wddm

> From my experience with refactoring the entire `IRenderEngine`, I have a solution:
> 
> Screw this (in `ControlCore.cpp`):
> 
> ```c++
>  _renderer
> ```

>

>  _renderEngine

I'm not going to ask Pankaj to further modify the **Renderer** interface in this pull request. It **might** be the right thing to do, but moving that function down will cost us changes in all 5 renderers PLUS code in conhost PLUS code in Terminal and the WPF control.
@DHowett  no i don't want it to move down to `IRenderEngine`, either. Check out my edit. I want it to be DX only, which helps all of us.

Oh, shit. I don't hate that. @miniksa what do you think?

I think we'd need to make sure we keep the features alive for the DPI change message, but...

The main risk is that we do eventually use a Renderer function that wants normal UpdateFont().

The thing I found in #10615 is that we have unfortunately stacked so many things inside `renderer.cpp`, even though some of are in fact very engine-specific. This harms the architecture severely, because it unnecessarily increase the coupling for a lot of code. This PR here, the `UpdateFont` dilemma we face, is just another example.

Let's stop this trend and make it right.

> We do not need durable process-lifetime storage for an intermediate map of feature tags and axes in conhost (not for VT, not for GDI, not for WDDM or BGFX, and conhost doesn't use DX today.)

The solution appears to be possible...
The API to set font features/axes is only called by WT and never by conhost. If the setter API is called the font feature `std::vector`s are generated eagerly. If the getter for features/axes is called we return the corresponding `std::vector`. If the DxRenderer asks for such information before the setter was called we can lazily initialize the `std::vector` with the default features/axes if necessary.
As such, as far as I can see, we don't actually need to allocate any maps/vectors if this was running under conhost. The struct would only contain members conhost doesn't need, but I don't consider this an issue (see below why, if you're interested).

That said I don't have any strong opinions about it. Code can always be modified. 🙂

--- 

Some performance ramblings:

From a CPU's perspective the size of a structure is not a deciding factor for performance as only data that's actually read is loaded into the CPU's cache. A much much more important factor would be structure layout for instance (fields should be grouped by their relation, data accessed in predictable patterns, ...).
As such if we add hash-maps or vectors to a structure that's common between all renderers, the only downside would be an increase in memory usage (namely 64 (?) bytes per map). But on the other hand 64 bytes could be considered a rounding error, when conhost can consume up to 200MB of memory in more extreme cases... 🤔

In my opinion the commonly taught coding aspects of "separation of concerns" and "each behavior, one class" continue to loose importance, as CPUs get faster and IDEs get better. Nowadays we don't have to be as mindful how many bytes we use for class instances. Copying memory occurs at over 100GB/s. But accessing memory in patterns that the CPU _just doesn't like_ and throws a hissy-fit about it... that's the real thing that needs to be considered nowadays in my opinion.

As such I wouldn't mind putting things into `FontInfo` if you say they technically "naturally" belong there.
In fact I will probably (personally) continue to strive for combining all rendering related data into a single "render data" class, no matter whether the renderer needs that particular data.
The performance saved by having less switching logic and virtual calls, will almost certainly outweigh the performance cost of prematurely allocating vectors, maps, etc.

issue_context.title: Request: Support for Font Width Variants
issue_context.body:
Some fonts have multiple width variants.  [Iosevka](/be5invis/Iosevka) from @be5invis, for example, has an Extended variant.  Terminal should support the use of such variants.

Currently:
```
"fontFace": "Iosevka SS04"
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/708461/81503142-d84e9600-9296-11ea-865a-862401d6bcdc.png)

But when asking for the Extended variant, Terminal falls back to a default font — Consolas for me.
```
"fontFace": "Iosevka SS04 Extended"
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/708461/81503165-00d69000-9297-11ea-84a7-b83cea64f16f.png)

I propose support for width variants either through `fontFace` or through a new `fontWidth` profile configurable.

Please add this feature request to @be5invis's epic for similar issues, #1790.

To further explain it, there are currently 3 layers of abstraction (top-down):

1. User Settings | Font human-readable structure
2. DxFontInfo | DWrite font structure
3. DxFontRenderData | DWrite font render-related structure

This list will always contain the default features. 

The reason for this is that we _always_ call `SetFeatures` when `UpdateFont` gets called, and `SetFeatures` will reinitialize the feature vector (with the default features), and then add the ones provided by the user. We have to do it this way because we have no way of knowing whether the user deleted features, so we always need to clear the vector and reinitialize it
